entry_point: After Intermediate MPC (Maths, Physics, Chemistry)
required_exams: AP EAPCET (Engineering stream) for AP govt/private colleges; JEE Main + JEE Advanced for IITs/NITs/IIITs outside the state quota system; GATE later for M.Tech/PSU jobs
eligibility: Pass Intermediate MPC with ~45% aggregate (General) / ~40% (SC/ST) for AP EAPCET; JEE Main has no minimum-marks eligibility bar beyond passing Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, Maths. Typical duration: 4 years.
govt_private_options: Govt: JNTU Kakinada/Anantapur/Gurajada Vizianagaram and their affiliated Govt colleges; IITs, NITs, IIITs (via JEE, outside AP EAPCET). Private: Large number of private engineering colleges across AP (Vignan's, KL University, VIT-AP, SRM-AP, Amrita, GITAM, etc.) admitting via AP EAPCET rank or their own management/NRI quota seats
next_step: Campus placement into IT/core industry, GATE for M.Tech/PSU recruitment, MBA (via CAT/MAT) for management roles, or the UPSC Engineering Services Exam (ESE/IES - age 21-30, 33 with OBC relaxation) for Central govt technical services, or APPSC for state engineering posts
source: vedantu.com AP EAPCET 2026 guide (see Entrance Exams tab); NTA JEE Main info bulletin; blog.madeeasy.in / pwonlyias.com UPSC ESE 2026 eligibility (verified Sept 2026)

entry_point: After Intermediate BiPC
required_exams: NEET-UG (mandatory single entrance exam for all medical admissions in India)
eligibility: Intermediate BiPC (Physics, Chemistry, Biology) pass; NEET minimum marks: 50th percentile General, 40th percentile SC/ST/OBC; minimum age 17 years
govt_private_options: Govt: Govt medical colleges in AP (e.g. Andhra Medical College, Guntur/Kurnool/Siddhartha Medical Colleges) via NEET counselling - low fees, highly competitive seats. Private: Private medical colleges in AP (NRI/management quota seats carry substantially higher fees, often Rs 15-25 lakh/year) - admission still requires a valid NEET score
next_step: Register with AP Medical Council to practice, OR pursue NEET-PG for MD/MS specialisation. NExT (National Exit Test), meant to eventually replace NEET-PG/FMGE as the licensing exam, has been postponed by the NMC to roughly 2028-2029 (mock tests are running in the meantime) - not yet a real near-term requirement as of Sept 2026
source: dbuu.ac.in NEET UG 2026 guide; educationvibes.in / shiksha.com NExT postponement coverage (verified Sept 2026)

entry_point: After Class 12 (any stream, incl. CEC/HEC/MEC)
required_exams: CLAT (UG) for National Law Universities; AP LAWCET (Andhra Pradesh Law Common Entrance Test) for AP-based law colleges
eligibility: Class 12 pass, any stream; no fixed minimum marks specified in CLAT notification (verify each cycle); AP LAWCET similarly requires Class 12 pass
govt_private_options: Govt: National Law Universities (via CLAT, all-India) and Govt-run/university law colleges in AP (via AP LAWCET, conducted by Sri Padmavati Mahila Visvavidyalayam, Tirupati, on behalf of APSCHE). Private: Private law colleges in AP and elsewhere, many affiliated to state universities, admitting via LAWCET or management quota
next_step: Enrol with the Bar Council, take the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) to practice, OR pursue judiciary exams (APJS - AP Judicial Services) OR corporate law / litigation / LLM & academia
source: law.careers360.com CLAT 2027 guide; pw.live / collegeadmission.in AP LAWCET 2026 pages (verified Sept 2026 - conducting body confirmed as Sri Padmavati Mahila Visvavidyalayam)

entry_point: After any Bachelor's degree
required_exams: UPSC Civil Services Examination (CSE): Prelims (objective) -> Mains (descriptive) -> Personality Test/Interview
eligibility: Graduate degree from a recognised university (final-year students may also apply); age 21-32 years as on 1 Aug of exam year (relaxation for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD/ex-servicemen); General category gets 6 attempts, OBC 9 attempts, SC/ST unlimited within the age window
govt_private_options: Govt: Sole route: UPSC (Govt of India) - no private equivalent; coaching institutes (govt and private) only help with preparation, not the exam itself. Private: N/A (the exam itself has no private-sector equivalent); private coaching institutes (various, fees vary widely) support preparation
next_step: Allocation to IAS/IPS/IFS or other Central Services based on rank and preference; posting, training at LBSNAA (Mussoorie) or respective service academies, then a career in public administration
source: insightsonindia.com UPSC 2026 notification guide

career_name: State Civil Services (AP Group services via APPSC)
entry_point: After any Bachelor's degree
required_exams: APPSC Group 1 (and Group 2/3/4) exams: Preliminary -> Main (multiple papers) -> Interview
eligibility: Bachelor's degree (specific stream sometimes required depending on post, e.g. Commerce degree for Treasury posts); age limits vary by post (commonly 18-42 years for many Group 1 posts, narrower for specific technical/police posts, e.g. 21-28 for Assistant Commissioner)
govt_private_options: Govt: Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission (APPSC) - state government recruitment for Deputy Collector, DSP, Assistant Commissioner, Treasury Officer, and other state administrative posts. Private: N/A (state government exam; private coaching institutes support preparation only)
next_step: Posting into AP state administrative, police, revenue, or allied services; promotion track within state cadre; some posts allow later transfer/promotion toward IAS/IPS via limited promotion quota
source: adda247.com APPSC Group 1 2026 notification guide

entry_point: After Bachelor's degree (B.A./B.Sc./B.Com.) or Intermediate (for D.Ed route)
required_exams: D.Ed (2-year Diploma in Elementary Education, for Classes 1-5) or B.Ed (1-year, for Classes 6-8 and above) -> AP TET (Teacher Eligibility Test) -> AP DSC (Departmental Selection Committee recruitment exam) for government posts
eligibility: Primary teachers: Intermediate with ~45% marks + D.Ed (2-year), or ~50% marks + 4-year B.El.Ed; Upper-primary teachers: Bachelor's degree with ~45% marks + 1-year B.Ed
govt_private_options: Govt: Government/ZP/Municipal schools in AP via AP DSC recruitment (AP TET score carries a 20% weightage in the final DSC merit list). Private: Private (unaided/CBSE/ICSE) schools recruit directly - AP TET/DSC not mandatory for most private-school posts, though many private schools still prefer TET-qualified candidates
next_step: Government School Teacher / Secondary Grade Teacher (SGT) / School Assistant post via DSC; promotion track to Headmaster and further to educational officer cadre with seniority and further qualification (e.g. M.Ed)
source: careerpower.in AP TET 2026 guide; teachersbadi.in AP DSC references

entry_point: After Class 12 (via NDA) or after graduation (via CDS)
required_exams: NDA (National Defence Academy exam, via UPSC) after Class 12, OR CDS (Combined Defence Services exam, via UPSC) after graduation - both followed by SSB Interview and medical tests
eligibility: NDA: Class 12 pass (Army wing, any stream) or Class 12 with Physics & Maths (Air Force/Navy wings); age within a specific ~2-year window, max ~19.5 years, unmarried. CDS: Bachelor's degree, age typically 19-24 years depending on wing/entry
govt_private_options: Govt: Sole route: Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) exams leading to National Defence Academy / Indian Military Academy / Naval Academy / Air Force Academy - no private equivalent. Private: N/A (defence commissioning has no private-sector equivalent); private coaching academies support preparation only
next_step: Commission as an officer in the Indian Army, Navy, or Air Force; career progression through defence service ranks with promotions, further specialised training, and pension benefits on completion of service
source: competition.careers360.com NDA eligibility guide (also see 'AP Post-Inter Entrance Exams' tab)

entry_point: After Class 12 (Foundation route) or after graduation (Direct Entry route)
required_exams: ICAI CA Foundation -> CA Intermediate -> 2-year Articleship (practical training) -> CA Final -> ICAI membership
eligibility: Foundation: Class 12 pass (any stream, commerce preferred), minimum ~4 months' study period before the exam; Direct Entry (skips Foundation): Commerce graduate with ~55% marks, or non-commerce graduate with ~60% marks
govt_private_options: Govt: N/A - CA is a professional qualification regulated by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), a statutory govt-recognised body, not a college degree; both govt and private-sector jobs are open to qualified CAs. Private: Private coaching/CA classes (numerous institutes in AP, e.g. Vijayawada/Vizag/Guntur) support exam preparation; articleship is typically served under a private practising CA firm
next_step: Enrol as a Chartered Accountant with ICAI; career as an independent practitioner, or in audit/tax/consulting firms, corporate finance (CFO track), or government roles (e.g. Indian Audit & Accounts Service via UPSC uses a related exam)
source: pw.live CA Course Details 2026 guide

entry_point: After any Bachelor's degree
required_exams: IBPS PO/Clerk (for most public-sector banks) or SBI PO/Clerk (State Bank of India, separate exam) - Prelims -> Mains -> Interview (PO) or Prelims -> Mains (Clerk)
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university; age 20-30 years for PO (relaxation for SC/ST/OBC/PwD/ex-servicemen)
govt_private_options: Govt: Public-sector banks (SBI, Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank, Union Bank, etc.) via IBPS or bank-specific exams - the dominant govt-adjacent route for banking careers. Private: Private-sector banks (HDFC, ICICI, Axis, etc.) recruit via their own campus/lateral hiring processes, not through IBPS
next_step: Posting as Probationary Officer/Clerk in a public-sector bank; promotion track through bank management grades (Officer -> Manager -> Senior Manager -> AGM and beyond) based on seniority, internal exams, and performance
source: competition.careers360.com IBPS PO 2026 exam guide

entry_point: After Intermediate/Class 12 (MPC with Maths, or equivalent with Maths)
required_exams: NATA (National Aptitude Test in Architecture), conducted by the Council of Architecture (CoA) - some institutes also accept JEE Main Paper 2
eligibility: Class 12 pass with Physics, Chemistry, Maths (PCM); minimum aggregate in PCM ~50% for General/OBC, ~45% for SC/ST (sources conflict on the exact current cutoff - CoA lowered it at some point but the reported figure varies 45-50% across trackers as of Sept 2026, re-verify on nata.in before applying); minimum age 17 years
govt_private_options: Govt: Govt-run schools of architecture / architecture departments at state and central universities, admission via NATA/JEE counselling. Private: Numerous private architecture colleges across AP and nationally, admitting via NATA score
next_step: Register with the Council of Architecture (COA) to practice as an architect; further options include M.Arch specialisation, urban planning, or independent practice/firm employment
source: engineering.careers360.com NATA 2026 exam guide

entry_point: After Intermediate MPC or BiPC
required_exams: AP EAPCET (Pharmacy stream)
eligibility: Intermediate MPC or BiPC pass with Physics, Chemistry, and Maths/Biology; qualifying marks similar to other AP EAPCET streams (~45% General, ~40% SC/ST)
govt_private_options: Govt: Govt/Govt-aided pharmacy colleges in AP via AP EAPCET counselling. Private: Numerous private pharmacy colleges across AP, admitting via AP EAPCET counselling or management quota
next_step: Register with the Pharmacy Council of India/State Pharmacy Council to practice; career as a retail/hospital pharmacist, OR pursue M.Pharm/Pharm.D for clinical/research roles, OR roles in pharmaceutical manufacturing and drug regulatory affairs
source: vedantu.com AP EAPCET 2026 guide (Pharmacy stream; also see 'AP Post-Inter Entrance Exams' tab) - unverified: exact AP EAPCET Pharmacy stream cutoff, needs follow-up

entry_point: After Intermediate BiPC
required_exams: NEET-UG (used for B.Sc Nursing admission at many institutions, alongside some state/institution-specific nursing entrance tests)
eligibility: Intermediate BiPC pass with Physics, Chemistry, Biology; NEET minimum marks as per category (same as MBBS eligibility bar); minimum age typically 17 years
govt_private_options: Govt: Govt nursing colleges attached to Govt medical colleges in AP, admission via NEET-based counselling. Private: Private nursing colleges across AP, admission via NEET score or institution-specific process
next_step: Register with the Andhra Pradesh Nurses and Midwives Council (APNMC) to practice (mandatory, renewed every 5 years per Indian Nursing Council rules); career as a staff nurse in govt/private hospitals, OR pursue M.Sc Nursing for specialisation/teaching roles, OR opportunities in overseas nursing employment
source: dbuu.ac.in NEET UG 2026 guide; hmis.ap.nic.in / bhavyagyan.in APNMC registration pages (verified Sept 2026 - council name and abbreviation confirmed as APNMC)

entry_point: After Intermediate MPC or BiPC
required_exams: B.Sc (3 years) -> M.Sc (2 years) -> CSIR-NET or GATE (qualifying exams for research fellowships/PhD admission) -> PhD (typically 4-5 years)
eligibility: Intermediate MPC/BiPC pass for B.Sc admission (institution-specific entrance or merit-based, varies by university); CSIR-NET requires a Master's degree (or final-year Master's students may apply provisionally) in the relevant science subject, with minimum 55% marks (General/EWS) or 50% (OBC-NCL/SC/ST/PwD/Third Gender); JRF applicants must be under 30 as of 1 July of the exam year
govt_private_options: Govt: Govt universities and institutions (e.g. Andhra University, central universities, IISc/IITs for integrated programmes) offering B.Sc/M.Sc/PhD; CSIR-NET qualified candidates are eligible for Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) stipends at govt institutions. Private: Private universities/colleges also offer B.Sc/M.Sc programmes, generally with tuition fees (no direct private equivalent for CSIR-NET/JRF, which is a government fellowship route)
next_step: Academic/research career as a Scientist (CSIR labs, ISRO, DRDO, and other govt research bodies) or Professor (after PhD, via qualifying exams like SET/NET for lectureship), OR private-sector R&D roles in pharma/biotech/IT
source: CSIR-NET/GATE -> PhD pathway, general knowledge; pw.live / competitivecracker.com CSIR NET 2026 eligibility pages (verified Sept 2026 for marks/age criteria - category-specific relaxations can shift per notification, re-check before a real application)

entry_point: After Intermediate - MPC (B.Tech route) or after Class 12 any stream with Maths (BCA route)
required_exams: AP EAPCET (Engineering - CSE/IT/AI-ML/Data Science branches) for B.Tech; university/college-specific merit or entrance test for BCA
eligibility: B.Tech route: Intermediate MPC pass, same AP EAPCET qualifying marks as core Engineering (~45% General, ~40% SC/ST); BCA route: Class 12 pass with Mathematics, usually merit-based. Typical duration: B.Tech: 4 years; BCA: 3 years (often followed by MCA, 2 years, for those without a B.Tech)
govt_private_options: Govt: JNTU-affiliated Govt/Govt-aided engineering colleges (CSE/IT/AI&DS) via AP EAPCET counselling; a small number of Govt degree colleges offer BCA. Private: Very large number of private engineering colleges across AP offer CSE/IT/AI-ML/Data Science branches; private colleges/universities also offer BCA (3 years) as a non-engineering alternative into software roles
next_step: Campus placement into IT services/product companies, OR further study (M.Tech/MS abroad), OR govt IT cadre via UPSC/APPSC technical posts, OR entrepreneurship; BCA graduates often pursue MCA before core software roles
source: aurogroup.ac B.Tech CSE 2026 guide; ritroorkee.com Career Opportunities After B.Tech CSE 2026 guide - unverified: BCA-specific AP admission body name, needs follow-up

entry_point: After Intermediate - BiPC (or MPC for some Agricultural Engineering seats)
required_exams: ICAR AIEEA (UG) for ICAR/all-India seats, and/or AP EAPCET - Agriculture stream for AP state-quota seats
eligibility: Intermediate BiPC (or MPC for B.Tech Agricultural Engineering) pass; ICAR AIEEA minimum marks ~50% General, ~45% SC/ST. Typical duration: 4 years for B.Sc (Hons) Agriculture/Horticulture/Forestry and B.Tech Agricultural Engineering; B.V.Sc & AH (Veterinary) typically 5.5 years including internship (exact AP-specific duration not independently verified)
govt_private_options: Govt: Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) and Sri Venkateswara Veterinary University (SVVU) Govt colleges in AP, via AP EAPCET-Agriculture and/or ICAR AIEEA counselling. Private: A smaller number of private agriculture/veterinary colleges affiliated to state agricultural universities also exist, admitting via the same entrance exams
next_step: Govt jobs in state Agriculture/Horticulture/Animal Husbandry departments, ICAR research institutes, or agricultural extension services; OR private sector roles in agribusiness/agro-processing/veterinary practice; OR further study (M.Sc/PhD)
source: collegedekho.com ICAR AIEEA 2026 guide - unverified: ANGRAU/SVVU AP-specific seat matrix and B.V.Sc duration, needs follow-up

entry_point: After Class 12 (any stream) for UG design programmes
required_exams: NIFT Entrance Exam (B.Des/B.FTech at National Institute of Fashion Technology) or NID DAT (National Institute of Design Entrance Exam)
eligibility: Completed or appearing Class 12; maximum age 24 years as of 1 August for NIFT UG programmes. Typical duration: NIFT: B.Des and B.FTech typically 4 years each (exact programme-wise duration split not independently verified); NID UG programmes also typically 4 years
govt_private_options: Govt: NIFT (20 campuses nationwide, a statutory Institute of National Importance) and NID (Ahmedabad and other campuses) - both Central Government design institutes. Private: Numerous private design colleges/universities across India (and a smaller number in AP) admit via their own entrance tests or accept NIFT/NID scores
next_step: Placement into fashion/apparel/product design houses and brands, OR further study (M.Des), OR entrepreneurship (own design label/studio)
source: design.careers360.com NIFT 2026 guide - unverified: exact B.Des/B.FTech duration breakdown and NID DAT 2026-specific dates, needs follow-up

entry_point: After Class 12 (CSEET route) or after graduation (direct Executive entry)
required_exams: ICSI CSEET -> CS Executive Programme -> CS Professional Programme -> ~21 months practical training -> ICSI membership
eligibility: CSEET: Class 12 pass, any stream; CS Executive: pass CSEET, OR graduates/post-graduates may enter directly without CSEET by paying an exemption fee. Typical duration: Approximately 4-5 years total from Class 12 (CSEET + Executive ~8 months + Professional ~8 months + 21 months practical training), depending on exam attempts
govt_private_options: Govt: N/A - CS is a professional qualification regulated by ICSI, a statutory govt-recognised body, not a college degree. Private: Private coaching institutes support CSEET/Executive/Professional exam prep; practical training typically served under a practising CS or a corporate secretarial department
next_step: Enrol as a Company Secretary with ICSI; career in corporate compliance/governance roles, as an independent practising CS, or in-house company secretarial departments of listed companies
source: admitkard.com Company Secretary (CS) Course 2026 guide

entry_point: After Class 12 (Foundation route) or after graduation (direct Intermediate entry)
required_exams: ICMAI CMA Foundation -> CMA Intermediate (2 groups, 8 papers) -> CMA Final -> practical training -> ICMAI membership
eligibility: Foundation: Class 12 pass, any stream; Intermediate: pass Foundation, OR bachelor's degree in any discipline except Fine Arts, OR pass ICSI Executive/ICAI Intermediate. Typical duration: CMA Intermediate alone takes ~8-10 months of dedicated study; total duration from Class 12 to full qualification (incl. Foundation, Final, practical training) not fully specified in the source - unverified, needs follow-up
govt_private_options: Govt: N/A - CMA is a professional qualification regulated by ICMAI, a statutory govt-recognised body, not a college degree. Private: Private coaching institutes support Foundation/Intermediate/Final exam prep across AP
next_step: Enrol as a Cost & Management Accountant with ICMAI; career in cost/management accounting, corporate finance, or govt roles (e.g. Indian Cost Accounts Service)
source: mileseducation.com CMA Intermediate Course guide - unverified: exact total duration and practical training length, needs follow-up

entry_point: After Class 12 (RRB NTPC UG posts) or after graduation (SSC CGL and RRB NTPC Graduate posts)
required_exams: SSC CGL: Tier-I -> Tier-II (Papers I/II/III, final merit); RRB NTPC: CBT 1 -> CBT 2 -> Typing Skill Test (where applicable) -> Document Verification -> Medical Exam
eligibility: SSC CGL: Bachelor's degree (some posts have subject-specific requirements); age 18-27 to 18-32 years depending on post. RRB NTPC (UG posts): Class 12 pass, age 18-30 years (category-wise relaxation). Typical duration: SSC CGL: Tier-I typically Aug-Sep, Tier-II typically Dec, of the same recruitment year; RRB NTPC: CBT stages spread across several months per cycle
govt_private_options: Govt: Ministries/departments of the Govt of India (Finance, Intelligence Bureau, Defence, Communications, enforcement agencies, via SSC CGL) and Indian Railways zonal railways (via RRB NTPC) - both exclusively government routes. Private: N/A (government recruitment exams with no private-sector equivalent); private coaching institutes support preparation only
next_step: Posting as Inspector/Auditor/Accountant (SSC CGL) or Commercial-cum-Ticket Clerk/Accounts Clerk/Junior Clerk/Trains Clerk (RRB NTPC UG); promotion through departmental seniority, internal exams, further qualification
source: oliveboard.in SSC CGL Eligibility 2026 guide; testbook.com RRB NTPC UG 2026 guide

entry_point: After Class 12 (any stream, with English as a core subject)
required_exams: NCHMCT JEE (National Council for Hotel Management and Catering Technology Joint Entrance Examination)
eligibility: Passed or appearing in Class 12 with English as a core/compulsory subject; no upper age limit under the New Education Policy. Typical duration: 3 years (BSc HHA)
govt_private_options: Govt: 21 Central/State Institutes of Hotel Management (IHMs) via NCHMCT JEE counselling - includes IHM Hyderabad, the nearest Govt IHM serving AP students. Private: NCHMCT-affiliated private hotel management institutes also admit via the same NCHMCT JEE score
next_step: Placement into hotel chains (govt-linked ITDC properties or private chains like Taj/Oberoi/Marriott) as management trainee, OR further study (MSc/MBA in Hospitality), OR entrepreneurship
source: adda247.com NCHMCT JEE guide (2025-cycle dates cited; 2026-specific dates and govt-vs-private placement split unverified, needs follow-up)

entry_point: After Intermediate (any stream, though MEC/CEC/HEC/BiPC commonly chosen)
required_exams: BA/BSc Psychology (3 years, merit-based) -> MA/MSc Psychology (2 years) -> for clinical practice: M.Phil Clinical Psychology (2 years) via an RCI-recognised entrance exam (e.g. NIMHANS or CIP Ranchi)
eligibility: UG: Intermediate pass, any stream, merit-based admission (no dedicated national entrance exam identified); Clinical specialisation: Master's degree in Psychology required before M.Phil Clinical Psychology entrance. Typical duration: BA/BSc 3 years + MA/MSc 2 years (5 years for a Master's); +2 years M.Phil Clinical Psychology for licensed clinical practice
govt_private_options: Govt: Government universities/institutes offering BA/MA Psychology (e.g. Andhra University); premier govt clinical-psychology institutes include NIMHANS Bangalore, IHBAS Delhi, CIP Ranchi. Private: Numerous private colleges/universities offer BA/MA Psychology; private practice common after RCI registration, alongside corporate HR and school-counsellor roles (growing under NEP 2020)
next_step: Without RCI registration, a psychology graduate cannot legally practice clinical assessment/therapy in India; RCI-registered psychologists work in govt hospitals, private practice, schools, or corporate HR; PhD enables academic/senior clinical roles
source: brighttutorials.in How to Become a Psychologist in India (2026) guide - unverified: AP-specific psychology/counselling entrance exam or state licensing body, needs follow-up
